healthcareSystem: State-funded universal system for residents. Tourists must pay out-of-pocket or use travel insurance. Private clinics offer higher-quality care.
qualityNotes: Major cities (Moscow, St. Petersburg) have excellent private clinics with English-speaking staff. Public hospitals vary widely in quality. Rural healthcare is limited.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 8am-9pm; 24/7 pharmacies (аптека 24 часа) available in cities
pharmacyTips: Look for 'Аптека' (Apteka) signs — pharmacies are very common. Pharmacists may not speak English but can often identify medications by generic name. Many drugs available OTC in Russia that require prescriptions elsewhere.
commonOTC: activated charcoal (активированный уголь — popular local remedy)
prescriptionRules: Many medications that require prescriptions in Western countries are available OTC in Russia. Antibiotics and strong painkillers technically require a prescription but enforcement varies. Foreign prescriptions are not accepted — visit a local clinic for a Russian prescription if needed.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is a controlled substance. Bring documentation if carrying codeine-based medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Strong opioids (tramadol, morphine)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Carry a doctor's letter and prescription. Quantities above personal use may be confiscated.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (some benzodiazepines, ADHD medications)
restrictedMeds.note: Some stimulant-based ADHD medications are banned. Bring documentation for any controlled psychiatric medication.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English and Russian (if possible) listing all medications with generic names and dosages. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, bring the original prescription. Amounts exceeding a 90-day supply may require customs declaration.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Travel insurance is required for Russian visa applications and may be checked at entry.
travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance is mandatory for obtaining a Russian visa. Ensure your policy meets the minimum coverage requirement (typically €30,000 / $35,000). Private clinics in Moscow and St. Petersburg offer high-quality care but are expensive.

recommended: Tick-borne Encephalitis (for rural/forest areas, especially Siberia)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for entry. Tick-borne encephalitis is a real risk in forested areas from spring through autumn.

waterNotes: Tap water in Moscow and St. Petersburg is technically treated but often has a metallic taste and may cause stomach upset. Drink bottled or filtered water. In smaller cities and rural areas, always use bottled water.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety in restaurants is generally good in major cities. Be cautious with street food and dairy products outside cities. Avoid uncooked salads in smaller establishments. Wash fruits and vegetables before eating.
medicalTourismNote: Russia attracts medical tourists for dental care, eye surgery (LASIK), and some cosmetic procedures, particularly in Moscow and St. Petersburg where costs are lower than Western Europe.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Russia. Emergency 112, pharmacy tips, hospital info, vaccination advice, and travel insurance requirements.

hospitals.name: European Medical Center (EMC)
hospitals.notes: Premium international clinic. Full emergency services, direct insurance billing. Western-trained staff.

hospitals.name: American Medical Clinic
hospitals.notes: English-speaking clinic popular with expats and tourists. General practice and emergency care.

hospitals.name: Botkin Hospital
hospitals.notes: Major public hospital with emergency department. Limited English — bring a translator or translation app.

hospitals.name: MEDSI Clinic
hospitals.notes: Large private clinic network with modern facilities and some English-speaking doctors.

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care in Moscow and St. Petersburg. Many private dental clinics with modern equipment.
dentalCare.costRange: $30-80 for a consultation; $50-200 for fillings; $40-150 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Dental tourism is popular — Russian private clinics offer quality care at lower prices than Western Europe. Many dentists in Moscow speak some English.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, visit a private dental clinic (стоматология). Most have walk-in emergency slots. Public dental clinics are available but may have long waits.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: No dedicated English-language crisis line — contact your embassy
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available in Moscow and St. Petersburg through international clinics (EMC, American Medical Clinic). Sessions typically $80-150.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services in English are very limited outside Moscow and St. Petersburg. Stigma around mental health remains in Russian culture. International clinics offer the best access for English-speaking travelers.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is improving but remains limited, especially outside Moscow. Many older buildings and metro stations lack elevators.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major private hospitals are wheelchair accessible. Older public hospitals may have limited accessibility.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Moscow Metro is adding elevators but many stations remain inaccessible. Newer stations are accessible. Buses in Moscow are increasingly wheelchair-friendly.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Plan routes carefully in advance. Moscow has improved significantly in recent years. St. Petersburg's historic buildings often lack accessibility features.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates. Masks are uncommon in public.
covidStatus.testing: PCR and rapid tests available at private clinics and labs. Cost: 1,500-4,000 RUB ($15-40).
covidStatus.notes: Russia lifted COVID entry restrictions. Testing is widely available at commercial labs like Invitro and Helix.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private clinics in Moscow often offer direct insurance billing for major international insurers. At other facilities, pay upfront and keep all receipts and medical documents (translated to English if possible). File claims with your insurer upon return. Request itemized bills and diagnosis codes.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private facilities. Public hospitals may provide emergency care at lower cost. Costs are significantly lower than Western Europe or the US.

medicalEvacuation.note: Moscow has world-class private hospitals. Evacuation from remote Siberian areas can be very expensive and logistically complex. Medical evacuation insurance is strongly recommended.
